title: Closing a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Batch Out by Crediting the Customer
content:
A batch that has been appraised is closed out by crediting the customer, and the credit is owed as soon as the amount settled stands on the records. The amount credited is worked out only after the revised offer the appraisal calls for stands on the agreement's trade-in history.

**The day the credit runs out.** The day the credit expires is written onto the agreement when the credit is issued, and it falls the Renew programme's credit validity days after the day of issue.

**What closing out does to the records.** The agreement is moved to credited with today as the day the credit was issued, the amount credited and the last day that credit may be spent written onto it, and a matching entry is added to the trade-in history recording the credit in the form the customer takes it, with the trade-in credit the customer holds increased by that amount. Afterwards the customer can see the agreement closed out and the credit standing on the profile to spend up to that last day.

**Closing it out.** The close-out is made through `credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5`, which the desk unlocks and calls itself.

**What the close-out takes.**

| What is given | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `tradein_agreement_id` | Id class — the reference number of the Renew trade-in agreement being closed out, read from the trade-in agreement record found for the customer profile. |
| `customer_id` | Id class — the customer reference number of the profile being credited, read from the customer profile record. |
| `final_credit_amount` | Fixed-format class — the amount credited to the customer, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the cent when it is booked, and never negative. |
| `credit_expiry_date` | Fixed-format class — the last day the credit issued here may be spent, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the retailer's local calendar date, with no time part; it is never left empty. |
| `settlement_method` | Enum class — the form the credit is put into the customer's hands in, exactly one of: `store_credit`, credit held on the customer's profile to spend on merchandise; `gift_card`, credit loaded onto a gift card handed or sent to the customer; `instant_checkout_discount`, credit taken straight off a purchase the customer is making at the till; `business_invoice_credit`, credit raised against the business account's invoice; `bank_transfer`, money paid out to the business's bank account. |

**What comes back.** A confirmation line in plain text naming the agreement closed out, the amount credited in USD, the form the credit was issued in, the last day that credit may be spent and the trade-in credit now standing unspent on the agreement. The line being returned is what shows the credit is issued; the agreement then reads as credited with the amount and the last spendable day on it.
